verses.text: In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam's rule, Abijah became king of Judah.
He ruled for three years in Jerusalem. His mother was Micaiah, daughter of Uriel from Gibeah. There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
Abijah went into battle with an army of four hundred thousand brave, chosen soldiers. Jeroboam lined up against him with eight hundred thousand chosen, strong, brave soldiers.
Abijah stood on Mount Zemaraim, in the hill country of Ephraim, and shouted, "Listen to me, Jeroboam and all Israel!
Don't you know that the LORD, the God of Israel, gave the kingdom of Israel to David and his sons forever, by a covenant that cannot be broken, a covenant of salt?
But Jeroboam son of Nebat, a servant of Solomon son of David, rose up and rebelled against his master.
Worthless, wicked men gathered around him and stood against Rehoboam son of Solomon, when Rehoboam was young and timid and could not stand up to them.
Now you plan to fight against the LORD's kingdom, which is in the hands of David's sons. You are a huge crowd, and you have with you the gold calves that Jeroboam made to be your gods.

Didn't you drive out the LORD's priests, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites? Didn't you make your own priests like the peoples of other lands do? Anyone who comes with a young bull and seven rams to make himself holy can become a priest of gods that are not gods at all.
But as for us, the LORD is our God, and we have not left him. Our priests who serve the LORD are sons of Aaron, and the Levites help them in their work.

Every morning and every evening they burn offerings and sweet incense to the LORD. They put the holy bread on the pure table and take care of the gold lampstand and its lamps, to light them every evening. We obey the LORD our God, but you have left him.

Look, God is with us as our leader. His priests are here with trumpets to sound the battle call against you. People of Israel, do not fight against the LORD, the God of your ancestors, because you will not win."
But Jeroboam had sent soldiers around to hide behind Judah's army. So his main army was in front of Judah, and the hidden soldiers were behind them.
When the men of Judah looked around, they saw they were being attacked from the front and the back. They cried out to the LORD, and the priests blew the trumpets.
Then the men of Judah gave a battle shout. As they shouted, God defeated Jeroboam and all Israel in front of Abijah and Judah.
The Israelites ran away from Judah, and God handed them over to them.
Abijah and his army killed a great many of them. Five hundred thousand chosen men of Israel fell dead.
So the Israelites were defeated at that time, and the people of Judah won, because they trusted in the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
Abijah chased Jeroboam and took towns from him: Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephron, with their villages.
Jeroboam never became strong again while Abijah was alive. The LORD struck him down, and he died.
But Abijah grew powerful. He married fourteen wives and had twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
Everything else Abijah did, how he lived and what he said, is written in the writings of the prophet Iddo.
